data.turoyo: <...> Kubʕono w kmətraǧyono mənux d marfət Sefdin Aġa. <...>
data.translation: <...> Ich verlange von dir und flehe dich an, dass du Ssêfdîn-Agha freilässest <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: first-person feminine -yono, mən-addressee and d-requested action.

data.translation: <...> Da habe ich die Statthalter angefleht; aber sie haben ihn nicht losgelassen; <...>

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: first-person agent and plural m-addressees; no invented distinction from ordinary petition.

data.turoyo: <...> Lakan kmətraǧeno minux aḏ̣ḏ̣arbo ʕafu. Hul uʕdo u mede, d səmme ʕafu. Lo saymat mede appe! <...>
data.translation: <...> Aber ich bitte dich: Diesmal verzeih ihnen! Verzeihe ihnen das, was sie bis jetzt gemacht haben, und tue ihnen nichts! <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: explicit min-person and requested pardon ʕafu; the exact noun-versus-directive analysis is left open.

data.turoyo: Li emo məqqaṣ d mətraǧela mu gawrayḏa. Səmla lo səmla, čara lawi mine.
data.translation: Soviel auch die Mutter ihren Gatten bat; was sie auch anstellte, es war nichts bei ihm zu erreichen.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: feminine petitioner, husband m-addressee and persistent unsuccessful petition.

data.turoyo: Omər: "Tamo disa mətraǧeli mi ḥurmayḏi w man naʕimayḏi məlli: "Bavo, bu baxtaṯxu w d aloho toxu aʕmi!" Mərre: "Ašər, lo koṯina.""
data.translation: Da bat ich wieder meine Frau und meine Kinder und sprach: Bei eurer und Gottes Ehre! Kommt doch mit mir! Sie sprachen: Wir kommen nicht.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell, reaching five: coordinated wife and children as m-addressees, followed by the request itself.

data.turoyo: Aq=qadišani, i=daʕwaṯṯe komitaqblo m u=moraṯṯe. Hani komətraǧən m u=moraṯṯe w komamṭən i=tərtaṯe.
data.translation: Das Gebet der heiligen wird von ihrem Herrn erhört. Sie bitten ihren Herren und bringen die Kuh nach Hause.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell, reaching five: ko-form with m-addressee, contrastable with already-cited l-addressee at 90/11.
The inherited 90/11 example already has l u=alohaṯṯe; 90/15 has m u=moraṯṯe in the same saints-petition context, so the current me-only government is incomplete.

summary: All 11 occurrences remain trǧy I sense 1. The entry's lexical t-containing mətraǧ- shape is retained; Arabic V etymology does not turn this ordinary Turoyo I entry into a synchronic Detransitive.
The person petitioned normally has me-/m-/mən- coding. 90/11 has l u=alohaṯṯe whereas 90/15 uses m u=moraṯṯe for the same divine addressee role; the government gloss is widened, with no new sense.

Requested content is a d-action clause at PrS 4/4, a following quotation at 33/83 and 63/314, or a pardon request at 56/93. The unvocalized ʕafu there may be a requested noun or a quoted directive; its nominality is not established by word order alone.

First-person feminine kmətraǧyono and masculine kmətraǧeno preserve source y-variation; Preterit mətraǧeli/əla and plural mətraǧalle take l-series agent endings. The Imperativ at 64/59 already exists and is not duplicated.
Permitted lookup confirms rǧy II mraǧele/mraǧe is a separate, cross-referenced entry. Shared meaning does not license moving these t-containing tokens into rǧy II or merging roots.
Existing citations 33/83, 44/119, 62/82, 64/59 and 90/11 are retained without duplicate examples. No special lexicalized collocation or light-verb combination is established.
At 56/93 is ʕafu a zero-marked requested noun 'pardon', a direct command, or shared between the petition and quoted request? Preserve the edition translation without resolving the syntax by fiat.
Is l-addressee versus me-addressee a productive alternation or a lexical/dialect choice? 90/11 and /15 provide a close contextual comparison.
Do mətraǧyono versus mətraǧeno reflect ordinary personal morphology, dialect or transcription? The sources are retained as printed.
What distinction, if any, exists between trǧy I and cross-referenced rǧy II beyond the t-containing form? The supplied overlap supports no new sense.
